loveLanguage.modeCourtDesc: Fifteen questions, and you know which language speaks to you most.
loveLanguage.modeCompletTitre: The full test with precise results
loveLanguage.modeCompletDesc: All thirty questions, to see your five languages ranked from first to last.
loveLanguage.palierTexte: Your results are ready. You can also keep going: the more you answer, the clearer the gap between your five languages gets.
loveLanguage.q1: You get home after a day when everything went wrong. Your partner is already there. What would help you most?
loveLanguage.q1a: Sitting down together and getting to tell them everything, without being interrupted
loveLanguage.q1b: A long hug by the door, before I've even taken my jacket off
loveLanguage.q1c: One simple sentence: “You did what you could, I'm proud of you”
loveLanguage.q1d: Dinner already made, and nothing left to do for the rest of the evening
loveLanguage.q1e: A little treat on the table, bought with me in mind
loveLanguage.q1f: Half an hour of quiet on my own, before we talk about anything
loveLanguage.q2: Your partner has a free hour and wants to spend it making you happy. You'd rather have:
loveLanguage.q2a: The paperwork that's been piling up for weeks finally sorted
loveLanguage.q2b: A letter about everything they love about me
loveLanguage.q3: You've just had great news: a job, a passed exam, a project accepted. That same evening, what would you love most?
loveLanguage.q3a: A bottle or a small gift to mark the occasion
loveLanguage.q3b: Celebrating at a restaurant, just the two of us
loveLanguage.q3c: Having nothing to handle all evening: no shopping, no cooking, no dishes
loveLanguage.q3d: A hug so tight my feet leave the ground
loveLanguage.q3e: Finding out they've already told their whole family, beaming with pride
loveLanguage.q4: It's Sunday morning and nothing is planned. What would make it perfect?
loveLanguage.q4a: Staying curled up together under the covers for another hour
loveLanguage.q4b: A long breakfast, talking about everything and nothing
loveLanguage.q4c: Getting up to find the kitchen tidy and the dishwasher already emptied
loveLanguage.q4d: Croissants from my favorite bakery, picked up just for me
loveLanguage.q4e: A sweet little note left on my pillow
loveLanguage.q4f: Having the morning to myself: a book, a bath, a walk on my own
loveLanguage.q5: Which of these moments would hurt you the most?
loveLanguage.q5a: A cutting remark about me in front of our friends
loveLanguage.q5b: Asking three times for the same bit of help and nothing happening
loveLanguage.q5c: A forgotten birthday, without even a small something
loveLanguage.q5d: Talking about something important while their eyes stay on their phone
loveLanguage.q5e: Moving in for a cuddle and feeling them pull away
loveLanguage.q6: Of these two gestures, which would touch you more?
loveLanguage.q6a: The book I mentioned once, in passing, waiting for me on the table
loveLanguage.q6b: The tap that's been dripping for months, finally fixed
loveLanguage.q7: You're stuck in bed with a fever. What comforts you most?
loveLanguage.q7a: Everything handled without me: the pharmacy, the meals, the house
loveLanguage.q7b: A cool hand on my forehead
loveLanguage.q7c: Having them next to me all evening, even if we're just watching a show
loveLanguage.q7d: A little care package: tea, a magazine, chocolate
loveLanguage.q7e: Sweet texts, even from the next room
loveLanguage.q8: It's the anniversary of the day you met. What would touch you most?
loveLanguage.q8a: A letter going back over everything we've been through since
loveLanguage.q8b: A gift that plays on a joke only the two of us get
loveLanguage.q8c: A night of tenderness, never letting go of each other
loveLanguage.q8d: An evening planned from start to finish, with nothing for me to organize
loveLanguage.q8e: Retracing together the walk from our first date
loveLanguage.q9: For your birthday, you'd rather have:
loveLanguage.q9a: A whole day together, phones off
loveLanguage.q9b: A carefully chosen present I'd never have thought of
loveLanguage.q10: You've had an argument, and things are starting to calm down. What helps you most to move on?
loveLanguage.q10a: An apology with real words, not just a “fine, whatever”
loveLanguage.q10b: Curling up against each other, even if it's a bit awkward
loveLanguage.q10c: Doing something together to put it behind us: a walk, a movie
loveLanguage.q10d: Seeing the chore that started it all done, without a word
loveLanguage.q10e: A flower left on my nightstand, like a white flag
loveLanguage.q10f: Time to cool down on my own before we talk about it again
loveLanguage.q11: When you want to show your partner you love them, what comes most naturally to you?
loveLanguage.q11a: Clearing some time so we can be together
loveLanguage.q11b: Telling them, writing it to them, sending them messages

loveLanguage.q11e: Making their life easier: fixing a problem, taking a chore off their hands
loveLanguage.q12: It's been a busy week, and you have twenty minutes together before sleep. You'd rather spend them:
loveLanguage.q12a: Wrapped up in each other, not necessarily talking
loveLanguage.q12b: Talking, each of you telling the other about your day
loveLanguage.q13: You're at a party at some friends' place. What makes you melt coming from your partner?
loveLanguage.q13a: A hand resting on my back every now and then
loveLanguage.q13b: Bringing me food and drinks without my having to ask
loveLanguage.q13c: Compliments about me, said in front of everyone
loveLanguage.q13d: Leaving with a slice of cake they saved for me
loveLanguage.q13e: Slipping out onto the balcony for five minutes, just the two of us
loveLanguage.q14: Over time, what would make you doubt your partner's love?
loveLanguage.q14a: Evenings side by side, each on our own screen
loveLanguage.q14b: Months without a single kind word
loveLanguage.q14c: Always having to cope on my own when everything piles up

loveLanguage.q15b: A hand on my waist and a kiss on the neck

loveLanguage.q16d: Walking hand in hand through a city we don't know
loveLanguage.q16e: A bracelet from a market stall, bought for me
loveLanguage.q16f: Keeping one morning to myself, so it's even better to meet up again after
loveLanguage.q17: For Valentine's Day, you'd rather have:
loveLanguage.q17a: The thing I was eyeing in a shop window without saying a word
loveLanguage.q17b: A handwritten declaration, full of true things about us

loveLanguage.q18a: “I'm so proud of you, I just wanted to tell you”
loveLanguage.q18b: “I called the garage about your car, it's sorted”

loveLanguage.q18d: “Tonight, phones off, just the two of us?”
loveLanguage.q18e: “Can't wait for tonight, I just want to curl up against you”
loveLanguage.q19: Which of these sentences from your partner would hurt you the most?
loveLanguage.q19c: “Stop fishing for compliments, you know what I think”
loveLanguage.q19d: “Not this weekend either, I've already made other plans”
loveLanguage.q19e: “A present? What for, it's not a special occasion”
loveLanguage.q20: You're setting off on a long car trip together. You'd rather have:
loveLanguage.q20a: A hand on my leg for a good part of the drive
loveLanguage.q20b: A bag of my favorite snacks, packed just for the road
loveLanguage.q21: On a first date, what makes you fall for someone?
loveLanguage.q21a: Their full attention, phone away from start to finish
loveLanguage.q21b: A flower or a book they brought for me
loveLanguage.q21c: Everything taken care of: the place, the booking, the ride home
loveLanguage.q21d: Natural contact, a hand brushing against mine
loveLanguage.q21e: Words that make me feel one of a kind
loveLanguage.q22: It's an ordinary Tuesday evening. What would make it nice?
loveLanguage.q22a: A flower picked up on the way home, put in a glass
loveLanguage.q22b: A compliment dropped in passing, about nothing in particular
loveLanguage.q22d: Finding the dishes done before I've even thought about them
loveLanguage.q22e: Their feet against mine on the couch
loveLanguage.q23: On a weekday, just before leaving in the morning, you'd rather have:
loveLanguage.q23a: My coffee made and my lunch packed
loveLanguage.q23b: A real kiss, not a quick peck on the way out
loveLanguage.q24: You're at a long family meal that's a bit heavy going. What helps you get through it?
loveLanguage.q24a: A “you were perfect” whispered in my ear as we leave
loveLanguage.q24b: Knowing we're leaving early to finish the evening together
loveLanguage.q24c: Having nothing to manage: the drive, the gift for the hosts, when to leave
loveLanguage.q24d: Their fingers looking for mine under the table
loveLanguage.q24e: An ice cream bought on the way home, as a reward
loveLanguage.q24f: An hour on my own when we get home, to decompress
loveLanguage.q25: Your partner is having a bad week. What's your first instinct?
loveLanguage.q25a: Taking over whatever is weighing on them: meals, appointments, errands
loveLanguage.q25b: Keeping my evening free to listen to them
loveLanguage.q25c: Sending them messages to lift their spirits
loveLanguage.q25d: Lots of tender gestures: a hand in their hair, an arm around their shoulders
loveLanguage.q25e: Surprising them with something to take their mind off things
loveLanguage.q26: On a Saturday, your partner suggests two plans. You pick:
loveLanguage.q26a: “Let's head out for the whole day, just the two of us”
loveLanguage.q26b: “I'll do the shopping and the cleaning, you get some rest”
loveLanguage.q27: When you think about your relationship, which kind of memory comes back first?
loveLanguage.q27a: A letter or a declaration I still reread
loveLanguage.q27b: A slow dance in the kitchen, holding each other close
loveLanguage.q27c: A present that showed me I'd really been listened to
loveLanguage.q27d: A whole night spent talking until sunrise
loveLanguage.q27e: The time everything was taken care of while I was swamped
loveLanguage.q28: Your partner goes abroad for a month. After a week, what do you miss most?
loveLanguage.q28a: Having them close, falling asleep curled up together
loveLanguage.q28b: Their little everyday words, their compliments
loveLanguage.q28c: Our dinners and our evening talks
loveLanguage.q28d: Everything that got done around the house without me thinking about it
loveLanguage.q28e: Their little surprises, the things they'd bring back for me
loveLanguage.q28f: Not much yet: I'm enjoying having time to myself
loveLanguage.q29: What makes you feel most that you matter to your partner?
loveLanguage.q29a: Being told, for no particular reason, how much I matter
loveLanguage.q29b: Them canceling plans to spend the evening with me
loveLanguage.q30: Thirty years from now, which picture of your relationship would make you happiest?
loveLanguage.q30a: Still holding hands when we go for a walk
loveLanguage.q30b: Taking care of each other in the small everyday things
loveLanguage.q30c: Still surprising each other, even after all that time
loveLanguage.q30d: Having kept our rituals: morning coffee together, the Sunday walk
loveLanguage.q30e: Still saying “I love you” every day
loveLanguage.r_words_t: Your Love Language: Words of Affirmation
loveLanguage.r_words_d: For you, love is all about words. A sincere compliment, an “I love you” whispered at just the right moment, a sentence that recognizes your worth, that's what makes your heart sing. You need to hear what your partner feels, not just guess it. Words are the most tangible proof of love for you, because they require the other person to pause, reflect, and express what they truly feel. Silence, even when well-meaning, can sometimes feel cold or distant to you. A careless criticism can wound you deeply, precisely because words carry immense weight in your emotional world.
loveLanguage.r_words_a: Let your partner know that words matter to you, it's not superficial, it's simply how you receive love. Encourage little daily affirmations, messages throughout the day, even simple declarations. And in return, don't hesitate to express your own feelings with words too: your partner will learn by example.
loveLanguage.r_acts_t: Your Love Language: Acts of Service
loveLanguage.r_acts_d: For you, love is proven through actions, not speeches. When your partner takes on a task without being asked, anticipates your needs, or lifts a weight off your daily routine, that's when you truly feel loved. It's not about laziness or comfort, it's that in your view of love, to love means to act for the other person. Every concrete gesture is proof of attention and devotion. On the flip side, a partner who makes promises without following through or who lets all the responsibilities fall on your shoulders can make you feel like you don't matter.
loveLanguage.r_acts_a: Communicate clearly about what genuinely helps you, without expecting your partner to guess. Offer to exchange acts of service so the balance feels fair. And remember: if your partner has a different love language, their way of showing love might look different from what you expect. Learn to recognize those gestures too.
loveLanguage.r_gifts_d: Contrary to popular belief, this love language has nothing to do with materialism. For you, a gift is a symbol, it's proof that your partner thought of you, took the time to choose something that fits who you are. A little note slipped into your bag, a flower picked along the way, an object that recalls a shared memory, that's what truly moves you. What matters isn't the price tag, but the intention and thoughtfulness behind the gesture. A complete lack of these small tokens can leave you feeling invisible or forgotten in the relationship.
loveLanguage.r_gifts_a: Explain to your partner that it's the symbolic gestures that count, not the cost. Give them real examples of what makes you happy, what moves you. And don't hesitate to lead by example, offering small thoughtful surprises of your own. It creates a wonderful cycle of generosity and closeness in your relationship.
loveLanguage.r_time_d: For you, nothing beats time spent together. Not just being in the same room, but truly being present for each other, no phones, no distractions, with genuine and undivided attention. You need to feel that your partner actively chooses to spend time with you, that you are their priority. A walk together, a deep conversation, a shared activity, these are the moments where you feel connected and loved. On the other hand, a partner who's constantly distracted, cancels your time together, or is always glued to their phone can hurt you deeply.
loveLanguage.r_time_a: Create rituals for two that are non-negotiable: a weekly dinner date, a daily walk, a screen-free moment every evening. Explain to your partner that the quality of your time together matters just as much as the quantity. And when you're together, be fully present yourself, lead by example with the undivided attention you're looking for.
loveLanguage.r_touch_d: For you, physical contact is the most direct path to the heart. A gentle brush, a hand placed on your back, a spontaneous hug, holding hands while walking, these gestures connect you to your partner in a way that words alone can't reach. It's not just about sexuality, it's a deep need for closeness, warmth, and physical presence that reassures you and makes you feel loved. The absence of physical contact, even in a relationship that's loving in other ways, can create a sense of loneliness and emotional distance that's hard to put into words.
loveLanguage.r_touch_a: Talk openly with your partner about your need for physical touch, making clear that it goes far beyond sexual intimacy. Suggest moments of tenderness with no expectations: a morning hug, holding hands, an evening massage. If your partner is less tactile, find a rhythm together that works for both of you, without pressure, but with consistency.
loveLanguage.nuance_space_t: You also need time to yourself
loveLanguage.nuance_space_d: {{n}} times, you picked a moment just for you over a gesture from your partner. That takes nothing away from love: plenty of people need to recharge on their own, and take in the other person's affection better once they've had a breather. The risk is that your partner reads this need as distance. The simplest thing is to say it, for example: “I need half an hour of quiet, then I'm all yours.”
